Markdown is part of 10 of my public repositories, from 2013 to 2026.

What it was for: [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (6), [Knowledge](@/projects/knowledge.md) (2), [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (1) and [Media and art](@/projects/media.md) (1).

Most recently: [past](@/work/past.md); [tinder-nomics](@/work/tinder-nomics.md); [corvidae](@/work/corvidae.md).

1 of these projects runs as a live site.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses Markdown: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links Markdown to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
